:NUMALIGARH REFINERY LIMITED  A COMPANY INCORPORATED UNDER THE COMPANIES ACT  1956  Page
HAVING ITS REGD OFFICE AT 122A  CHRISTIAN BASTI  G S ROAD  GUWAHATI- 781005

ASSA Advocate for the Petitioner : MR. A CHAUDHURY Advocate for the Respondent : GA, ASSAM :: BEFORE ::
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PRASANTA KUMAR DEKA -O R D E R- 28.11.2019 Heard Mr. AD Choudhury, learned counsel for the petitioner and Ms. M Bhattacharjee, learned Additional Senior Government Advocate, Assam for the State respondents.
The petitioner was licensed by Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and on the basis of the said licence she was running her petrol depot at Nazira.

M/s BPCL through its engineering department directed its registered vendor M/s NK Enterprise for carrying out modifications and upgradation of the tank and other works in respect of the said petrol depot, M/s NRL Energy Station.

After completion of the said work necessary standardisation of the dispensers and the readings of the meters thereof dispensing petrol in the said depot was carried out by the Metrology department at Sivasagar and to that effect a certificate was issued in favour of the petitioner.
On 26.07.2018 the Sub-Divisional Magistrate cum Additional Deputy Commissioner, Nazira Sub-Division sealed the petrol dispensers of three dispensing units for investigation/corrective measures.
On 14.08.2018 the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL), Guwahati submitted the analytical report of the samples of the said petrol depot opining about water contents present in the said samples.
On 08.09.2018 the Inspector of Food & Civil Supplies Consumer Affairs, Nazira lodged an FIR against the petitioner before the Nazira Police Station.
The Nazira Police seized two documents which includes the forwarding report and the analysis report of the FSL, Guwahati.

On 13.12.2018 the Nazira police submitted charge-sheet before the court of Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate,
Nazira.

It would not be out of place to mention here that M/s BPCL through its letter dated 15.09.2018 Page No.# 3/6 informed the petitioner the cause of presence of water in the sample examined by the FSL, Guwahati as follows:-
"To The Dealer, M/s Basanta Energy Station, (M/s NRL Energy Station Nazira)
Nazira, Assam Subject: Water entry into underground tank of MS at the retail outlet.

Dear Madam, This is to inform you that BPCL, through its engineering Department,
M/S. Nrl Energy Station Nazira @ Basanta ... vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 28 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151507030/
2 had allotted a work order No 4506838572 dated 14.06.2018 to our registered vendor M/s NK Enterprise, for carrying out modifications and upgradations to the tank and pipelines of the retail outlet.
While the work was being carried out, due to issue in tank gaskets, water entered the underground tank.
If water seeps into the tank for any reason whatsoever, since it is heavier than the petroleum product, it will settle at the bottom of the tank.
On suction from the pump, which is from the lower end of the tank, the water is likely to enter the vehicles of the customers.
In line with this an incident occurred in the month of July wherein water had entered the underground tank in the retail outlet.
Adequate steps have been taken thereafter to rectify the defect and remove the water from the tank.
You are also advised to periodically check for water accumulation in underground tank using water detecting paste while checking the dips to avoid incidents in future.

Regards, Sd/-
P Mahanta Territory Manager (Retail) BPCL, Guwahati"

The said action on the part of the respondents is challenged before this court in this writ petition stating that the impugned action is without jurisdiction and in contravention of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 and the Assam Trade Article (Licence and Control) Order, 1982.

sentences.text: The respondent no. 4, the Inspector, Food and Civil Supplies Consumer Affairs Page No.# 4/6 department filed affidavit-in-opposition wherein it is stated that M/s BPCL vide its letter dated 14.08.2018 through its Manager, Sales (Retail), Guwahati informed the Additional Deputy Commissioner cum Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Nazira about the inspection of the depot and the cause of accumulation of water in the underground tank due to seepage during heavy rain and faulty fittings in the tank manhole and the rectifications thereon.

The Additional Deputy Commissioner cum Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Nazira vide its letter dated 26.07.2018 requested the Manager (Sales) to carry out a joint inspection/ verification of the depot to settle the issue but there was no response from the said M/s BPCL.
Subsequent thereto on 08.09.2018 after receipt of the FSL report opining that the samples failed to meet the BIS specifications for Motor Spirit, FIR was lodged at Nazira Police Station.

Since then the matter is under the judicial authority and as such the question of reopening of the sealed depot by the Additional Deputy Commissioner cum Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Nazira does not arise.

In the said affidavit-in-opposition the respondent deponent stated that only the petrol dispensers were sealed but the same were not in the mere opinion of the respondent officials but due to admission of the petitioner about the existence of impurities in the dispensed petrol.

Mr. Choudhury submits that on the basis of the FIR, Nazira Police Station charge- sheeted the petitioner as follows:-

sentences.text: "Charge or information, Nature of offence and circumstances connected with if so consise detail, and under what section of the Penal code charged.

The brief fact of the case is that on 26/07/2018 in the afternoon at around 4 PM, as per verbal complaint received from the public, the informant Md. Kamaluddin Ahmed, Inspector, Food, Civil Supplies & Consumer Affairs, Nazira, has taken samples from M/S Basanta Energy Petrol pump and send it to Gauhati FSL for examination, and after receipt the analysis report from FSL, it is found that the owner of the above petrol pump, Smt Minoti Bezboruah W/O (Lt) Horendra Bezboruah, resident of Nazira ward No 8, of Police station Nazira, and Manager Sri Biju Sarmah, S/O late Nila Kt Sarmah, resident of No - 02 Halaguri Gaon, Police Station - Sivasagar has done adulteration in the above mentioned petrol.

Accordingly,
the Informant has lodged a First Information Report and FIR was registered under section 7 of Essential Commodities Act and after investigation, I submitted Charge-sheet before this Hon'ble Court.
The witnesses mentioned in Column no 6 will prove the truth of the Ejahar.
Therefore, it is requested to send summon to the witnesses by fixing the trial day.
1 (one) seizure list, sketch-map, 2(two) bail bonds, FSL report are attached along with the First Information Page No.# 5/6 Report.
Sd/- illegible F/d to the Hon'ble SDJM Court of Nazira (M) Through the P.S.I Nazira Court.
Along with case diary, sketch map, seizure list, 2 (two) nos Bail Bond and Expert opinion of PSL report are enclosed here with.
Sd/- illegible"

As against the said charge sheet the learned court of Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Nazira vide order dated 17.05.2019 passed in PRC 12/2019 under section 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (State vs. Minati Bezbaruah and Biju Sharma)
discharged the petitioner holding that there exists no sufficient and cogent grounds to frame charge against the accused person under section 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 and the accused persons were discharged and set at liberty.
Referring to the said judicial order it is the submission of Mr. Choudhury that as the District Administration consisting the respondent officials lodged FIR, a duty was cast to take note of the order dated 17.05.2019 passed by the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Nazira and ought to have acted under the law.

sentences.text:
In addition to that Ms.
Bhattacharjee projected that there is an admission on the part of the petitioner, the licensee under M/s BPCL about the water content which is also one of the grounds for lodging the FIR.

However, Ms. Bhattacharjee fairly submits that as the FIR was lodged by the respondent officials for a judicial decision and as the petitioner is discharged there being no challenge to the judicial decision of the learned SDJM,
Nazira, the same would hold the field and the consequences thereafter.
Page No.# 6/6 I have given due consideration to the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.
The issue involved is whether there is a malpractice on the part of the petitioner.
Admittedly there was renovation works in the petrol depot and the same was carried out on the instruction of M/s BPCL.
The officials of M/s BPCL informed about the seepage of water into the newly made tank and the reasons were also informed to the Additional Deputy Commissioner cum Sub-Divisional Officer of Nazira.
In turn the said official of M/s BPCL as requested to be present in the petrol depot to carry out joint investigation which the said official failed.

As there was default on the part of the official of the M/s BPCL to take part in the verification as stated in the affidavit-in-opposition of the respondent no. 4, in my considered opinion, the District Administration had no other alternative keeping in view the FSL report and as per the set out procedure, FIR was lodged.

The same was duly considered by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Nazira and having gone through the facts and circumstances including the opinion and the causes of such seepage of water of M/s BPCL the petitioner was discharged.

As the issue involved had already been decided by the judicial court there is no further requirement of continuance of sealing the said three dispensers done on 26.07.2018 by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate cum Additional Deputy Commissioner, Nazira Sub-Division under Sl. Nos. MI823196, MI823213 and MI823216 Model No. TIQ 2442SSPN.

Accordingly, the respondent no. 3 is directed to remove the seal in the said dispensers immediately on the receipt of the certified copy of this order and with the said direction this writ petition stands disposed of.
Copy of the order dated 17.05.2019 passed by the learned SDJM, Nazira is kept on record.
